report.summary: The notification-worker is in an OOM crash loop: its in-process TemplateCache.put exhausts the 2Gi heap, the container is OOMKilled and restarted repeatedly, and throughput collapsed from about 30 req/s to about 6 req/s at 09:55 UTC while queue lag grew from about 4s to 947s. The likely origin is the v1.8.0 deploy of 2026-08-31, which added an in-process template cache, with the 2026-09-02 batch-size increase as a possible amplifier. Slow email-provider responses (degraded per the status page) are a contributing factor but do not explain the memory exhaustion. The shallow /health check stayed green throughout, so the crash loop was not surfaced by health checks.

root_cause.mechanism: v1.8.0 caches rendered templates in-process without a bound; heap grows until GC thrashes and the JVM throws OOM in TemplateCache.put, the container is OOMKilled and restarted repeatedly, and consumption collapses so the queue lag grows.
assumptions: Telemetry before 09:00 is unavailable, so the pre-09:00 memory trend is unknown.

ranked_hypotheses.mechanism: v1.8.0 caches rendered templates in-process without a bound; heap grows until GC thrashes and the JVM throws OOM in TemplateCache.put, the container is OOMKilled and restarted repeatedly, and consumption collapses so the queue lag grows.
assumptions: Telemetry before 09:00 is unavailable, so the pre-09:00 memory trend is unknown.

ranked_hypotheses.mechanism: Degraded eu-west latency on the email provider slows each send, lengthening processing time and holding heap-resident messages longer, which adds memory pressure and reduces drain rate.
assumptions: The status page reflects actual provider latency; no provider metrics were available.

ranked_hypotheses.mechanism: Send batch size raised 50 to 100 on 09-02 increases per-batch heap usage, pushing the already-leaking cache past the 2Gi limit sooner.
assumptions: Heap use scales with batch size.

observed_facts.statement: notification-worker queue_lag_s rose from about 4s (09:55) to 140.92s at 10:00 and 946.91s at 10:30.
notification-worker request_rate fell from 30.95 req/s (09:50) to 6.16 req/s (09:55) and stayed near 6 req/s through 10:30.
notification-worker memory_pct climbed from 81.04% at 09:00 to 99.13% at 09:50, dropped to 54.02% at 09:55, then rose again to 90.26% at 10:30.
notification-worker restarts counter went from 0 to 3 between 09:55 and 10:25.
Eight java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space errors were logged at TemplateCache.put(TemplateCache.java:57) between 09:54:22 and 10:25:28.
Container notification-worker-7c9d was OOMKilled (limit 2Gi) at 09:55:02, 10:10:16 and 10:25:14.
GC overhead warnings (92% of time in GC over 60s) appeared from 09:30:01 onward, before the first OOM error.
email-provider slow-response warnings (809ms, 697ms, then 2400ms) appeared from 09:08:51 onward; email-provider is reported degraded in eu-west.
Deploy v1.8.0 of notification-worker on 2026-08-31 10:00 introduced 'cache rendered email templates in-process'; a config change raised send batch size 50 -> 100 on 2026-09-02 08:00.
The notification-worker health check returned healthy (HTTP /health 200) at 10:28, and notification-queue was healthy too.

assumptions: Telemetry before 09:00 UTC is unavailable, so the memory trend since the 08-31 deploy cannot be confirmed directly.
The /health check is shallow and does not reflect OOM restarts or consumer throughput.
The OOMKilled container name (7c9d) belongs to the notification-worker deployment that processes the queue.
The email-provider status page reflects the actual degradation; email-provider has no metrics in this system.

inferred_conclusions.statement: The primary fault is unbounded in-process template caching in notification-worker v1.8.0, which leaks heap until OOM, causing restart loops, and the consumer stalls, producing the queue lag.
The email-provider slowdown is a contributing factor that slows per-message processing and raises memory pressure, but it is not the root cause of the OOM.
The 09-02 batch-size increase (50 to 100) likely raised per-batch heap use and may explain why the leak reached OOM now rather than earlier.
The platform node pool upgrade (09-03 01:00) is not implicated: the failure is confined to one service's heap and restarts, and no node-level signal was checked.

remediation.action: Roll notification-worker back to v1.7.x (pre-TemplateCache) or disable the in-process template cache, then confirm queue drain.
remediation.rationale: Stops the OOM restart loop that collapsed consumer throughput.

remediation.action: Temporarily revert send batch size from 100 to 50 while recovering.
remediation.rationale: Reduces per-batch heap pressure if the leak persists before rollback completes.

remediation.action: Watch the email-provider eu-west latency and consider failing over to the secondary provider if it persists.
remediation.rationale: Slow sends reduce drain rate once the consumer is stable.

remediation.action: Add a bounded (LRU/size-limited) template cache with a heap-usage test before redeploy.
remediation.rationale: Fixes the unbounded growth at TemplateCache.put.

remediation.action: Make the health check exercise consumer progress and restart count, not just HTTP 200.
remediation.rationale: The shallow health check stayed green during the crash loop.

remediation.action: Alert on OOMKilled restarts and GC overhead for notification-worker.
remediation.rationale: GC warnings started at 09:30, about 25 minutes before the first OOM.

open_questions: Why did memory climb only after 09:00 when v1.8.0 deployed 2026-08-31? Telemetry before 09:00 is not available.
Does the batch size change of 09-02 08:00 change the leak rate?
Is email-provider latency alone enough to explain the drop in throughput, or is the consumer dead for most of the period?
What is the email-provider status and its eu-west latency history? No metrics were returned for it.
